title: Monomachine Editor data contract, version 2 (MM OS 1.32B)
description: Plain-data documents between the Monomachine Editor page and the machine. Firmware units throughout. Cross-field limits (lock row count, offsets inside lengths, sorted locks) are enforced by elektronData::validate in C++, not here. See mm-data-contract.md.

oneOf.description: The standalone's audio and MIDI devices, shared with the Machinedrum Editor (data-contract.md 4.8)

flag.description: bit 3 of the play byte, meaning unknown, kept

range.description: octaves - 1 (the RNGE knob's 0-8, measured on the firmware)

trigs.description: synth tracks only: bit 0 AMP, 1 FLT, 2 LFO

noteEntry.description: [track, step, MIDI note]; [7, 63, 127] is an empty entry (0xffff), seen inside the count in factory data

trig.description: steps holding a trig (pitch, trigless or pitchless)

chord.description: steps with extra notes in chordNotes

page.description: SYN AMP FLT EFX LF1 LF2 LF3 MIDI

firmware.description: P6, contract version 2: what the firmware carries that the editor passes through untouched (dump format bytes, residue, opaque state, undecoded bytes). Readers also take version 1, where these members sit at the top level.

input.description: 0 NEIGHBOR 1 INP A 2 INP B 3 INP A+B 4-6 BUS AB/CD/EF

multiEnv.description: MULTI ENV, NRPN 0x40-0x45: ATK DEC SUS REL PORT and one more

trackMasks.description: Per-track bits (bit t = track t). MM-P4 corrected MM-P1's guess: mirror is the JOY mirror at 0x1d0; 0x2aa-0x2ac are key tracking LPF, HPF and PORTAMENTO (set = ALWAYS, clear = ONLY LEGATO).

multiTrig.description: MULTI TRIG (MM-P4, panel): mode 0 ALL TRK, 1 SPLIT KEY, 2 SEQ START, 3 SEQ TRNSP; timing 0 DIRECT, 1/16 2/16 4/16 8/16 16/16 32/16; splitKey the first key of the upper zone; splitTrack the first upper track, 0-based.

firmware.description: P6, contract version 2: what the firmware carries that the editor passes through untouched (dump format bytes, residue, opaque state, undecoded bytes). Readers also take version 1, where these members sit at the top level.

repeats.description: plays repeats + 1 times; on a loop: the count, 0 = infinite

firmware.description: P6, contract version 2: what the firmware carries that the editor passes through untouched (dump format bytes, residue, opaque state, undecoded bytes). Readers also take version 1, where these members sit at the top level.

controlIn.description: CONTROL IN (MM-P4, panel): tempoSync 0 INTERNAL, 1 EXT MIDI CLK; transport 0 IGNORE, 1 ACCEPT (MIDI Start/Stop).

firmware.description: P6, contract version 2: what the firmware carries that the editor passes through untouched (dump format bytes, residue, opaque state, undecoded bytes). Readers also take version 1, where these members sit at the top level.

lifecycle.description: P6: the machine's life as one value (deskCore::Lifecycle): the engine label and the input gate follow it.

capabilities.description: P6: what the engine can do, as data (deskCore::Capabilities), with what the editor does not do yet on any engine (the model's unsupported list) merged in. A page enables a control when can[name] is true and shows reasons[name] otherwise; a name it does not know is not allowed.

reasons.description: Why a capability is false: the text a disabled control shows.

engines.description: P6: the engine map (the plug-in's engine records), in menu order; empty for a desk outside the plug-in.

history.description: P6: the core's undo history (a gesture is one step).

modulators.description: App-only LFO and random sources and their links to the kit that plays (page -> plug-in, P6: run in the plug-in on the machine's steps, as the Machinedrum's).

param.description: DATA page * 8 + index (page 7 index 0: the level).

machine.description: Read-only machine state from the MM desk: current and queued pattern, kit and its working state, song, SYSEX RECV session, and the core's parts (P6: every member declared).

queued.description: LOAD PATTERN sent while playing: becomes current at the pattern end.

tempo.description: BPM from RAM; null while booting.

mutes.description: MM-P4: the machine's own mutes from RAM (made on its panel too), bit t = track t; null where the engine cannot read them (HW MIDI).

poly.description: MM-P4: POLY, the machine's audio mode (status 0x20); null until it answers.

desk.description: MM-P8: the machine's own sequencer state from RAM, as the Machinedrum's machine.desk.

oneOf.description: The firmware's pattern chain (BANK held + TRIG keys, manual 1-46; RAM 0x2bc2c4). One bank, each pattern once, loops. Played in pattern mode only: in song mode active can stay true while the song plays.

active.description: False after a pick (BANK + one TRIG) or STOP twice; a SysEx LOAD PATTERN leaves it (measured).

next.description: The entry the firmware queues next.

chain.description: null: not readable on this engine (HW MIDI).

bankGroup.description: The machine's BANK GROUP: 0 A-D, 1 E-H, -1 unknown (RAM 0x70000b).

state.description: The SYSEX RECV session's state (mmRecv); without the panel (HW MIDI) idle or waitingUser.

waiting.description: MM-P4, HW MIDI: messages that wait for the person to open SYSEX RECV (hwSend sends them).

loading.description: Background reading of the machine's slots: done counts the slots read plus those whose read was given up after its retries (failed), so done reaches total.

input.description: The machine takes the page's commands now (the lifecycle's gate).

midi.description: The firmware answers MIDI: loads run.

lifecycleText.description: What the lifecycle state means for the user, worded by the model.

contract.description: The page protocol's version (the contract document's): bumped when a member is renamed, removed or re-meant; adding one keeps it. A page reads it first.

slots.description: P6: how many documents of each kind (the model's kind records).

message.description: P6: every message the plug-in sends the Monomachine Editor page. Checked by mmDeskTest.

pending.description: The document shows an edit submitted to the machine and not yet read back (P6: pending, published merged over observed).

slot.description: The slot; for the working kit, the kit it was loaded from.

oneOf.description: A document: a stored slot (pattern, kit, song, global) or the kit that plays (workingKit, P6).

record.description: MM-P4: the recording mode (RAM): GRID RECORDING, LIVE RECORDING or off; null where the engine cannot read it.

songRow.description: 0.3.5: the song row the sequencer plays (RAM 0x2bdba1, md::MmTelemetry), null where the engine cannot read it. Meaningful while song.songMode is true and the machine plays.

oneOf.description: B-030: the host's tempo (a DAW's playhead, also while its transport is stopped), when it changed or the page is new. follows: the plug-in sets the machine to follow the host's clock (a DAW, not the standalone).
The firmware's own LCD: 128 x 64, one bit a pixel, rows of 16 bytes, base64 (P6: the same encoding as the MD's).
P7: the plug-in's verdict on a firmware file the user chose or dropped (checked, copied into the ROM folder; it never leaves the computer).
LOAD ROM: which firmware image the machine runs and where it is (the answer to romInfo). REMOVE only deletes inside the editor's ROM folder (inFolder).

Something the plug-in has for the user (a question or a warning), shown as the page's modal instead of a native alert; the button pressed goes back as noticeAnswer. The first button is the answer to a question, the last the safe one.

modal.description: false: a banner (no backdrop, the page usable under it; DESIGN-updates.md), not the dialog; absent: the dialog. A banner with no title and no text takes the banner away.

oneOf.description: P7, B-019: a .syx file the user chose or dropped, parsed by the plug-in: what it holds (per kind the items with their slot, name, format bytes, whether they overwrite data or play now) and what cannot be sent and why. It informs; the import sends the chosen messages to the machine as they are.

P7, B-019: an import's progress: before (the slots the editor has not read are read first), send (messages handed to the machine of the chosen ones), read (documents read back), done (with the report: per outcome a count, and a line for each item the machine did not take as in the file).
P7: an export to a .syx: written, or why not.

enabled.description: MIDI mapping (MIDI learn and the Control workspace) is on; the pages hide both unless true (mdmm::midiMappingEnabled, deskHost.h).

oneOf.description: P6: a question before something is lost. The page shows message with a confirm button; confirm resends command with force, which answers every question the command raised: a command that loses two things asks once, naming both (also). alternatives: other ways to go on, each its own button: the page sends its first commands, then command with force (loadKit: Save and load = saveKit first).

also.description: Other questions this one answers too (force answers all of them).

alternatives.description: Other ways to go on, each a button: label, and the commands sent before command with force.

oneOf.description: The standalone's audio and MIDI devices (host, mdAudioMidiLink; schema gm-audio/devices in md-data-contract.schema.json).
The window asks the page to open its AUDIO / MIDI panel.

command.description: Generated from the model's command table and the plug-in's (deskHost), P6: every command the page may send.
